children: Higher diesel prices and rising interest rates didn't derail FedEx's earnings. Third-quarter results topped Wall Street expectations. The stock still fell as investors work through guidance.
FedEx reported third-quarter earnings per share of $3.74 from sales of $22.9 billion. Wall Street was looking for earnings per share of $3.34 from sales of $22.7 billion.

Year ago comparisons are tough. FedEx spun off its less-than-truckload (LTL) business, FedEx Freight, in June. LTL businesses serve mainly industrial customers that don't need entire truckloads to move goods relatively short distances.

Guidance was nudged higher. For the full year, FedEx expects revenue growth of 12%, up from prior guidance of 11%. Earnings per share should be about $18.30. The midpoint of prior guidance was $17.60. Wall Street currently projects $17.68.

New guidance implies fourth-quarter earnings of about $6.33. Wall Street projects EPS of $6.58. But something doesn't match between full-year and quarterly numbers. Based on full-year estimates compiled by FactSet, analysts should have been looking for $5.92.

There is a mismatch between full-year and quarterly numbers. The spinoff of FedEx Freight could be the reason. (FedEx recently changed its fiscal year-end to December from May, which might be affecting data providers such as FactSet.)
Whatever the reason, shares were down 2.7% at $296.50 shortly after results were released.

Despite the drop, numbers look OK. Domestic revenue grew 10% year over year, with pricing and volumes helping. International revenue grew 17%. Adjusted operating income of about $1.2 billion was in line with Street estimates.
Through Wednesday trading, FedEx stock was up about 31% year to date, about 17 percentage points ahead of the S&P 500.
